issues.description: Preview API complects identity (node), value (preview payload), and time (when called) into one attached callable
issues.detail: preview_fn is bolted onto the node identity, but it produces values that have no temporal relationship to any run. The docs never say when the preview reflects — is it a snapshot of the last run, a hypothetical, or pure illustration? That conflation of node-identity, value, and time is the exact complecting to call out before the API ships.

issues.description: Seven typed preview classes are incidental complexity over what is fundamentally tagged data
issues.detail: JsonPreview, TablePreview, PlotlyPreview, MermaidPreview, ImagePreview, TextPreview, CustomPreview are seven near-identical shapes: a kind tag, a content blob, optional meta. This is a map with a :type key wearing a class costume. The docs should at least acknowledge the underlying data shape so users understand to_dict() is the actual contract.

issues.description: The closure workaround for data context reveals the API solved the wrong problem
issues.detail: The Using preview functions with data context section admits previews cannot see inputs or outputs, then teaches closure capture of stale sample_data defined at pipeline construction time. That sample is frozen at definition, not run time — a place-oriented hack. The honest design is a function from (inputs, outputs) to preview, or no preview at all.

issues.description: meta parameter is overloaded with two unrelated concerns
issues.detail: The docs explicitly say meta serves two purposes: general metadata and rendering configuration. That is complecting by documentation. A consumer cannot tell whether a key like language is descriptive or instructive. Splitting into meta and render_config would separate the concerns the docs already admit are separate.

issues.description: CustomPreview renderer_key couples pipeline code to a specific frontend's component registry
issues.detail: renderer_key identifies which frontend component should handle rendering ties node definitions to Kedro-Viz internals. The pipeline now carries knowledge of a UI component name. That is place-oriented in the worst sense: a string whose meaning lives in another repo, at another version, with no contract. Document the coupling explicitly or push it to a registration step.

issues.description: The question that should have been asked: why is this on the node at all
issues.detail: A preview is a function from some facts to a renderable value. It does not need to live on the node. The docs never justify why preview_fn is a node attribute rather than a separate registry keyed by node name. Coupling it to the node forces the experimental warning and the closure hack. A side table of previews would be simpler and decoupled.

review.summary: This is documentation for an API that has already shipped its complecting: preview_fn attaches a value-producing callable to a node identity without specifying its time semantics. The seven Preview classes are tagged data wearing class costumes, and the docs admit meta serves two unrelated jobs. The closure-based workaround for accessing data is the loudest signal that the API solved the wrong problem — previews want to be a function of inputs and outputs, not a context-free callable bolted to node identity. Before doubling down with more docs, the team should sit in the hammock and ask whether previews belong on the node at all, or in a separate registry keyed by node name with explicit time semantics.
